task: Publish checker facts for nested record values inside a main composition domain initializer.
observation: The main checker returned early when it recognized a domain construction binding, so an Inner(...) value nested in Harness(inner = Inner(...)) never passed through the normal expression checker. The domain graph already validates initializer purity and types, but it does not publish the exact EST constructor target/type facts needed by consumers. Traversing the retained named-value ExprId under main's SpecId gives the existing checker the exact child occurrence without source/name-based selection.
impact: The focused checker accepts the nested initializer and the EST dump contains the stable nominal declaration target on the nested constructor. Runtime validation is still blocked on this branch by a separate consumer constructor identity invariant; this is not engine-parity evidence.

./build/compiler/moss-dev run --interp tmp/team_a_nested_initializer/probe.moss (still fails downstream: checked constructor declaration has no unique ObjectType)
